blocks.text: SHENZHEN, China — The meeting among U.S. President Donald Trump, China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin on Thursday was the first-ever sit-down for the leaders of the three countries. They started with talk of a shared responsibility for keeping peace as the victors of World War II and as global powers. But post-meeting readouts by the three nations reflected more symbolism than substance. The “peace declaration” released after their meeting made no mention of Russia’s war in Ukraine or the U.S.-led war in Iran.
